words.en: to become less strong or intense
words.ex: The flood waters began to abate only after the rain stopped.
words.trick: A + BATE: the storm's anger 'bates' (lowers) like a deflating ball.

words.en: found everywhere
words.ex: Smartphones have become ubiquitous even in small villages.
words.trick: 'You-BIQ-uitous': YOU see it BIG everywhere.

words.en: lasting for a very short time
words.ex: Fame on social media is often ephemeral.
words.trick: Ephemeral sounds like 'a few minutes' — that's all it lasts.

words.en: a departure from what is normal or expected
words.ex: His poor score was an aberration in an otherwise excellent year.
words.trick: AB (away) + ERR (wander): wandering away from the usual path.

words.en: to hate something very strongly
words.ex: She abhors cruelty to animals.
words.trick: Ab-HORROR: you feel horror at what you abhor.

words.en: extremely bad, miserable or humiliating
words.ex: Many families in the drought area live in abject poverty.
words.trick: AB (down) + JECT (thrown): thrown down to the lowest state.

words.en: to shorten a text without losing its sense
words.ex: The publisher decided to abridge the novel for school students.
words.trick: A BRIDGE makes the road shorter — abridge makes the book shorter.

words.en: to choose not to do or have something
words.ex: Three members chose to abstain from the vote.
words.trick: AB + STAIN: stay away so you don't get a stain.

words.en: the ability to make good judgements quickly
words.ex: Her business acumen turned a small shop into a chain of stores.
words.trick: ACU = sharp (like acupuncture needles): a sharp mind.

words.en: refusing to change one's mind
words.ex: The coach was adamant that no player would skip practice.
words.trick: Adam-ANT: an ant that won't move off its path.

words.en: to warn or scold someone firmly
words.ex: The teacher admonished the students for talking during the test.
words.trick: ADMONISH sounds like 'add a punishment' — a warning first.

words.en: a difficult or unlucky situation
words.ex: She showed great courage in the face of adversity.
words.trick: ADVERSE + ITY: everything is adverse (against you).

words.en: friendly and easy to talk to
words.ex: The affable manager knew every employee by name.
words.trick: AFFABLE ≈ 'laugh-able' in a good way: easy to laugh with.

words.en: to make pain or a problem less severe
words.ex: The new flyover should alleviate traffic jams in the city.
words.trick: ALLEVIATE has LEV (lift, as in levitate): it lifts the burden.

words.en: having more than one possible meaning
words.ex: The question was so ambiguous that two answers seemed right.
words.trick: AMBI = both (ambidextrous): it points both ways.

words.en: to make something bad better
words.ex: The scheme aims to ameliorate the living conditions of farmers.
words.trick: A-MELIOR-ate: 'melior' is Latin for better.

words.en: pleasant and friendly
words.ex: Our amiable neighbour always helps with the shopping.
words.trick: AMI = friend (French 'ami'): friend-like.

words.en: something that is different from what is usual
words.ex: The auditor noticed an anomaly in the bank's accounts.
words.trick: A-NOMALY ≈ 'not normal-y'.

words.en: lack of interest or concern
words.ex: Voter apathy led to a very low turnout.
words.trick: A (without) + PATHY (feeling, as in sympathy): no feeling.

words.en: to calm someone by giving them what they want
words.ex: The company raised wages to appease the striking workers.
words.trick: AP-PEASE ≈ 'a peace': you buy a peace.

words.en: needing a lot of effort; very difficult
words.ex: The climb to the temple was long and arduous.
words.trick: ARDUOUS ≈ 'hard-uous': hard work.

words.en: willing to take bold risks
words.ex: It was an audacious plan to climb the peak in winter.
words.trick: AUDACIOUS has 'dacious' like 'daring'.

words.en: simple and strict, without comfort or luxury
words.ex: The monk lived an austere life in a small hut.
words.trick: AUSTERE ≈ 'a stern' life with no extras.

words.en: kind and wanting to help others
words.ex: A benevolent trader paid the school fees of poor children.
words.trick: BENE = good (benefit) + VOL = wish: wishing good.

words.en: honest and direct
words.ex: I want your candid opinion of my essay.
words.trick: A CANDID camera shows things as they really are.

words.en: changing mood or behaviour suddenly
words.ex: The capricious weather ruined our picnic twice.
words.trick: CAPRI = goat: as jumpy as a goat.

words.en: to persuade someone by flattery or gentle pressure
words.ex: The child tried to cajole his mother into buying ice cream.
words.trick: CAJOLE ≈ 'cage-hole': you sweet-talk the bird into the cage.

words.en: not caring about other people's feelings
words.ex: His callous remark upset the grieving family.
words.trick: A CALLUS is hard, dead skin — a callous person has a hard heart.

words.en: careful to consider risks before acting
words.ex: Be circumspect when sharing bank details online.
words.trick: CIRCUM (around) + SPECT (look): look all around first.

words.en: to force someone to do something by threats
words.ex: The witness said he was coerced into signing the statement.
words.trick: CO-ERCE ≈ 'co-force'.

words.en: clear, logical and convincing
words.ex: She made a cogent case for a shorter school day.
words.trick: COGENT ≈ 'cog' in a machine: every part of the argument fits.

words.en: too satisfied with oneself to try harder
words.ex: After topping the mock test, he became complacent and stopped revising.
words.trick: COMPLACENT ≈ 'comfortable place': too comfy to move.

words.en: to agree
words.ex: The other judges concurred with the chief justice.
words.trick: CON (together) + CUR (run): ideas running together.

words.en: to accept or overlook wrong behaviour
words.ex: The school will not condone cheating of any kind.
words.trick: CON-DONE: treating the wrong as 'done, forget it'.

words.en: easy to see or notice
words.ex: His bright red jacket was conspicuous in the crowd.
words.trick: CON-SPIC ≈ 'spectacle': everyone spots it.

words.en: in large amounts
words.ex: She took copious notes during the lecture.
words.trick: COPIOUS = many COPIES of something.

words.en: too ready to believe things
words.ex: Credulous customers fell for the fake lottery messages.
words.trick: CRED = believe (credit): believes everything.

words.en: mysterious and hard to understand
words.ex: He left a cryptic note that nobody could decode.
words.trick: CRYPT = hidden (crypto, cryptography).

words.en: to reduce or limit something
words.ex: The government plans to curtail wasteful spending.
words.trick: CUR-TAIL: cutting the tail short.

words.en: seeming difficult and scary
words.ex: Preparing for three exams at once is a daunting task.
words.trick: DAUNTING ≈ 'don't-ing': it makes you say 'don't try'.

words.en: to make someone or something very weak
words.ex: The long illness debilitated him for months.
words.trick: DE + BILITY: removes ability.

words.en: polite respect for someone's wishes or opinions
words.ex: In deference to his grandmother, he spoke softly.
words.trick: DEFER = step back and let the elder go first.

words.en: causing harm or damage
words.ex: Smoking has a deleterious effect on the lungs.
words.trick: DELETE-rious: it deletes your health.

words.en: working carefully and with steady effort
words.ex: A diligent student revises a little every day.
words.trick: DILIGENT ≈ 'dil laga ke': working with your whole heart.

words.en: careful not to cause embarrassment or reveal secrets
words.ex: Please be discreet about the surprise party.
words.trick: DIS-CREET ≈ 'discrete secret': keeps secrets separate.

words.en: the feeling that something is not worth respect
words.ex: She looked at the cheap gift with disdain.
words.trick: DIS + DAIN ≈ 'dis-deign': you won't deign to look at it.

words.en: doubtful; probably not honest or true
words.ex: Avoid investing in schemes that make dubious promises.
words.trick: DUBIOUS ≈ 'doubt-ious'.

words.en: speaking or writing fluently and persuasively
words.ex: Her eloquent speech moved the audience to tears.
words.trick: E + LOQU (speak, as in loquacious): speaks out well.

words.en: hard to find, catch or achieve
words.hi: मायावी, पकड़ में न आने वाला
words.ex: A gold medal remained elusive for the team.
words.trick: ELUSIVE = it ELUDES (escapes) you.

words.en: to decorate, or to add untrue details to a story
words.ex: He tends to embellish his travel stories.
words.trick: EM-BELL-ish: hang bells on it to make it fancy.

words.en: famous and respected in a field
words.ex: An eminent scientist will open the science fair.
words.trick: EMINENT stands out like a mountain 'eminence' (high ground).

words.en: a person or thing that is mysterious
words.ex: The origin of the ancient carvings remains an enigma.
words.trick: ENIGMA was the WWII secret-code machine — a famous mystery.

words.en: to destroy something completely
words.ex: The vaccination drive helped eradicate polio from India.
words.trick: E (out) + RADIX (root, as in radish): pull out by the root.

words.en: not regular or predictable
words.ex: The power supply in our area is erratic during summer.
words.trick: ERRATIC ≈ 'error-tic': full of errors and twitches.

words.en: to make a problem worse
words.ex: Burning crop stubble exacerbates air pollution in winter.
words.trick: EX-ACERB: acid (acerbic) poured on a wound.

words.en: so good that it should be copied
words.ex: The firefighter was praised for his exemplary courage.
words.trick: EXEMPLARY = fit to be an EXAMPLE.

words.en: much too high in price or amount
words.ex: The hotel charged an exorbitant price during the festival.
words.trick: EX + ORBIT: so high it's out of orbit.

words.en: a mistaken belief or faulty reasoning
words.ex: It is a fallacy that only toppers get good jobs.
words.trick: FALLACY = an idea that FALLS apart.

words.en: very weak
words.ex: He made a feeble excuse for missing class.
words.trick: FEEBLE ≈ 'fee-bly': too weak to pay the fee.

words.en: having or showing strong, sincere feeling
words.ex: She is a fervent supporter of girls' education.
words.trick: FERV = boil (as in fever): boiling with feeling.

words.en: careful not to spend much money
words.ex: By being frugal, the family saved for a new house.
words.trick: FRUGAL ≈ 'free-goal': goal is to keep money free (unspent).

words.en: having no useful result
words.ex: It is futile to argue with someone who will not listen.
words.trick: FUTILE ≈ 'few-tile': laying a floor with too few tiles — pointless.

words.en: fond of company; sociable
words.ex: Being gregarious, Ravi made friends on his first day.
words.trick: GREG = flock (as in congregation): loves the crowd.

words.en: behaving as if better than others
words.ex: The haughty officer refused to listen to the villagers.
words.trick: HAUGHTY ≈ 'high-ty': holds the nose high.

words.en: extremely evil or wicked
words.ex: The court called it a heinous crime and gave the maximum sentence.
words.trick: HEINOUS ≈ 'hate-us': a crime everyone hates.

words.en: unfriendly and ready to fight
words.ex: The crowd grew hostile when the match was cancelled.
words.trick: HOSTILE ≈ 'host + tile': a host who throws tiles at guests.

words.en: without any fault
words.ex: Her English pronunciation is impeccable.
words.trick: IM (not) + PECC (sin, as in peccadillo): not a single slip.

words.en: acting quickly without thinking
words.ex: His impetuous decision to quit cost him a good job.
words.trick: IMPETUS = a push: pushed into action before thinking.

words.en: continuing without stopping
words.ex: Incessant rain flooded the low-lying areas.
words.trick: IN (not) + CESS (cease): never ceases.

words.en: lazy; avoiding work
words.ex: The indolent clerk left every file for the next day.
words.trick: INDOLENT ≈ 'in-dole': living on the dole, not working.

words.en: certain to happen; unavoidable
words.ex: With so many errors, the team's defeat was inevitable.
words.trick: IN (not) + EVITABLE (avoidable): can't be avoided.

words.en: lacking flavour, interest or energy
words.ex: The hostel food was insipid and cold.
words.trick: IN (not) + SIP: not worth a single sip.

words.en: danger of loss or harm
words.ex: The strike put thousands of jobs in jeopardy.
words.trick: JEOPARDY ≈ 'leopard-y': a leopard nearby means danger.

words.en: showing good judgement
words.ex: Judicious use of water can prevent shortages in summer.
words.trick: JUDICIOUS = judges wisely, like a JUDGE.

words.en: lacking energy; sluggish
words.ex: The heat made everyone feel lethargic after lunch.
words.trick: LETHE was the river of forgetfulness: drowsy and slow.

words.en: clear and easy to understand
words.ex: The teacher gave a lucid explanation of compound interest.
words.trick: LUC = light (lucent): it sheds light.

words.en: wishing harm to others
words.ex: The villain gave a malevolent smile.
words.trick: MAL = bad (malfunction) + VOL = wish: wishing bad.

words.en: paying great attention to every detail
words.hi: अति सावधान, बारीकी से काम करने वाला
words.ex: A meticulous editor checks every comma.
words.trick: METICULOUS ≈ 'metric-ulous': measures every detail.

words.en: to make something less harmful or serious
words.ex: Planting mangroves can mitigate damage from cyclones.
words.trick: MITIGATE ≈ 'mitti (soil) gate': a soil wall that softens the flood.

words.en: ordinary and dull
words.ex: He wanted a break from the mundane routine of office work.
words.trick: MUNDANE ≈ 'Monday-ne': as dull as a Monday.

words.en: failing to take proper care
words.ex: The negligent driver was fined for jumping the signal.
words.trick: NEGLIGENT = one who NEGLECTS.

words.en: a person new to an activity
words.ex: As a novice, she practised basic moves for weeks.
words.trick: NOV = new (novel, nova).

words.en: no longer used; out of date
words.ex: Floppy disks became obsolete years ago.
words.trick: OBSOLETE ≈ 'absolutely old'.

words.en: stubbornly refusing to change
words.ex: The obstinate child refused to eat any vegetables.
words.trick: OBSTINATE ≈ 'obstacle': stands in the way and won't move.

words.en: suggesting that something bad will happen
words.ex: Dark clouds gathered in an ominous way over the sea.
words.trick: OMEN-ous: full of bad omens.

words.en: rich and luxurious
words.ex: The maharaja's palace was opulent, with gold-plated ceilings.
words.trick: OPULENT ≈ 'opal-ent': covered in opals.

words.en: to calm someone who is angry or upset
words.ex: The mother sang softly to pacify the crying baby.
words.trick: PACIFY: bring PEACE, like the calm Pacific.

words.en: the lack or scarcity of something
words.ex: The project stalled because of a paucity of funds.
words.trick: PAUCITY ≈ 'poor city': a city short of everything.

words.en: never ending or changing
words.ex: The Permanent Settlement fixed a perpetual land revenue in Bengal.
words.trick: PER (through) + PET (go): goes on and on.

words.en: seeming reasonable or likely to be true
words.ex: He gave a plausible reason for being late.
words.trick: PLAUS ≈ applause: an idea people would clap for.

words.en: dealing with things in a practical way
words.ex: A pragmatic approach is to solve the easy questions first.
words.trick: PRAGMATIC ≈ 'practical-matic'.

words.en: acting with care and thought for the future
words.ex: It is prudent to keep some savings for emergencies.
words.trick: PRUDENT ≈ 'provident': provides for the future.

words.en: long-lasting bitterness or resentment
words.ex: They settled the dispute without rancour.
words.trick: RANCOUR ≈ 'rancid': feelings gone sour.

words.en: not saying much about one's thoughts or feelings
words.ex: The actor is reticent about his personal life.
words.trick: RETICENT ≈ 'reti-silent': stays silent.

words.en: able to recover quickly from difficulties
words.ex: The resilient fishermen rebuilt their boats after the cyclone.
words.trick: RE-SILIENT ≈ 'rubber band': it springs back.

words.en: very careful to be honest and correct
words.ex: The scrupulous cashier counted every note twice.
words.trick: SCRUPLE = a tiny pebble in the shoe — it bothers your conscience.

words.en: happening at irregular intervals
words.ex: There were sporadic showers across the state.
words.trick: SPORADIC ≈ 'spores': scattered here and there.

words.en: strict and precise
words.ex: The RBI introduced stringent rules for digital lending.
words.trick: STRING pulled tight: no slack allowed.

words.en: holding on firmly; determined
words.ex: Her tenacious effort finally got her selected as a PO.
words.trick: TEN (hold, as in tenant) + ACIOUS: holds on tight.

words.en: of little value or importance
words.ex: Don't waste time arguing over trivial matters.
words.trick: TRIVIA = small facts that don't matter.

words.en: to prove that someone was right or not guilty
words.bn: নির্দোষ প্রমাণ করা, ন্যায্যতা প্রতিপাদন করা
words.hi: निर्दोष सिद्ध करना, सही साबित करना
words.ex: The new evidence vindicated the accused worker.
words.trick: VINDICATE ≈ 'win-dicate': you win the case.

words.en: likely to change suddenly and unpredictably
words.ex: Share prices remained volatile throughout the week.
words.trick: VOL = fly (volley): flies off in any direction.

words.en: great energy or enthusiasm for a cause
words.ex: The volunteers worked with great zeal to clean the river bank.
words.trick: ZEAL ≈ 'zeal-ous' fans who cheer loudest.
